ventures.name: SBE Aquafarm
ventures.orgType: Youth-led social enterprise (unregistered — Eric operates independently, co-founded with Syliah Kagiiga)
ventures.coFounder: Syliah Kagiiga — petroleum geology engineer, GLF Restoration Steward 2025-26
ventures.model: Converts abandoned/hazardous clay-mining pits into managed fishpond ecosystems: Convert (consolidate pits, restore hydrology), Surround (native tree planting, habitat corridors), Employ (women from female-headed households, out-of-school youth), Hand Over (12-month ownership transition to community).
sdgAlignment: SDG 8 Decent Work and Economic Growth
SDG 14/15 Life Below Water / Life on Land (wetland ecosystem)
ventures.fundingHistory: Purpose Earth grant application submitted (USD $8,000 requested, 18-month expansion phase). GLF Restoration Stewards program mentorship. Actively exploring microfinance and certification pathways.
ventures.idealOpportunityProfile: Wetland/ecosystem restoration grants, aquaculture/fisheries innovation funds, youth-led environmental social enterprise fellowships, gender-and-environment funds, small grants (<$25k) open to individuals/informal community enterprises, GLF/CIFOR-ICRAF-adjacent restoration networks, safe-water and drowning-hazard-reduction funders, food security & nutrition funders in East Africa.

ventures.name: SBE FBT (Fermented Bed Technology)
ventures.tagline: A circular pig-waste economy for smallholder farmers
ventures.orgType: Pilot project — unregistered, run by Eric with technical supervisor Ronnie
ventures.model: Fermented Bed Technology (FBT) piggery system that manages pig waste on-site through microbial fermentation, cutting odor/runoff pollution, reducing water use, and turning waste into a reusable input — a circular, low-cost alternative to conventional piggery waste management for smallholder farmers.
materialsBuilt: Field reference PDF for on-site technical supervisor
ventures.idealOpportunityProfile: Circular-economy and waste-to-value challenge funds, livestock/agritech innovation grants, smallholder farmer productivity funds, WASH (water/sanitation) funders, climate-smart agriculture fellowships, small pilot/proof-of-concept grants open to individuals.

eligibilityPriorities: Open to individuals or informal/unregistered ventures (not strictly requiring NGO/company registration)
East Africa / Uganda / Sub-Saharan Africa geographic scope, or open globally
Wetland restoration, aquaculture, circular economy, smallholder agriculture, gender & environment, or youth social enterprise themes
Grant, fellowship, prize, or challenge-fund format (not loans/equity unless explicitly relevant)
Award size roughly $500 - $50,000 is the practical sweet spot for current venture stage, though larger fellowship-style opportunities are still worth tracking
writingVoice: Direct, concrete, evidence-led. Leads with what has already been demonstrated (pits converted, hectares restored, households reached) before projecting forward. Avoids charity framing; frames the ventures as self-sustaining enterprises. Centers community ownership and named individuals (e.g., Agnes, Grace) as proof points.
